title: OCPP - Weak Authentication in OCPP 1.6
description: OCPP 1.6 does not mandate mutual authentication between charging stations and central systems. Basic authentication (username/password) over WebSocket is optional and often not implemented, allowing unauthorized devices to connect.
mitigation_strategies: Upgrade to OCPP 2.0.1 with Security Profile 3
Use VPN tunnels for OCPP communication
Enable TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites
detection_methods: Monitor for unauthorized charging station connections
defensive_actions: Upgrade to OCPP 2.0.1 with Security Profile 3
Use VPN tunnels for OCPP communication
Enable TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites
countermeasures: Upgrade to OCPP 2.0.1 with Security Profile 3
Use VPN tunnels for OCPP communication
Enable TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites
impact: OCPP 1.6 does not mandate mutual authentication between charging stations and central systems. Basic authentication (username/password) over WebSocket is optional and often not implemented, allowing unauthorized devices to connect.

title: OCPP - Lack of Message Integrity in OCPP 1.6
description: OCPP 1.6 does not provide built-in message signing or integrity verification. Attackers performing man-in-the-middle attacks can modify OCPP messages (e.g., RemoteStartTransaction, ChangeConfiguration) without detection.
impact: OCPP 1.6 does not provide built-in message signing or integrity verification. Attackers performing man-in-the-middle attacks can modify OCPP messages (e.g., RemoteStartTransaction, ChangeConfiguration) without detection.

title: OCPP - OCPP 2.0.1 Security Profile Downgrade
description: OCPP 2.0.1 defines three security profiles (1: Unsecured, 2: Basic Auth, 3: TLS with client certificates). If not properly configured, systems may downgrade to lower security profiles, negating security improvements.
mitigation_strategies: Enforce Security Profile 3 in all deployments
defensive_actions: Enforce Security Profile 3 in all deployments
countermeasures: Enforce Security Profile 3 in all deployments
impact: OCPP 2.0.1 defines three security profiles (1: Unsecured, 2: Basic Auth, 3: TLS with client certificates). If not properly configured, systems may downgrade to lower security profiles, negating security improvements.

title: ISO_15118 - Plug & Charge Certificate Validation Issues
description: ISO 15118 Plug & Charge relies on X.509 certificate chains for vehicle authentication. Improper certificate validation (e.g., not checking revocation, accepting expired certificates, weak signature algorithms) can allow unauthorized vehicles to charge.
mitigation_strategies: Check certificate revocation lists (CRL) or OCSP
Implement certificate pinning for root CAs
defensive_actions: Check certificate revocation lists (CRL) or OCSP
Implement certificate pinning for root CAs
countermeasures: Check certificate revocation lists (CRL) or OCSP
Implement certificate pinning for root CAs

title: ISO_15118 - TLS Configuration Weaknesses
description: ISO 15118-20 mandates TLS 1.2+ for secure communication between EV and EVSE. Weak TLS configurations (e.g., supporting TLS 1.0/1.1, weak cipher suites like RC4, CBC mode) expose communications to attacks.
mitigation_strategies: Use only strong cipher suites (AEAD modes)
defensive_actions: Use only strong cipher suites (AEAD modes)
countermeasures: Use only strong cipher suites (AEAD modes)
impact: ISO 15118-20 mandates TLS 1.2+ for secure communication between EV and EVSE. Weak TLS configurations (e.g., supporting TLS 1.0/1.1, weak cipher suites like RC4, CBC mode) expose communications to attacks.

title: Modbus_TCP - Lack of Authentication in Modbus TCP

Deploy firewall rules restricting Modbus access
